transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Hello, Doctor. Well, I suppose what brings me in is that I’ve gotten stuck doing these... little routines lately. Like, I find myself washing my hands again every time I handle my wrist brace. I actually had to start wearing this brace because my joints have been acting up. My wife thinks it's from all the years I spent hunched over my desk at the university—I was in the history department, you see, spending hours upon hours in the archives. Fascinating stuff, really, the way 19th-century paper degrades if it isn't kept in a properly climate-controlled room. The smell of old books is just... well, anyway, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, the routines. So I wash my hands, and then I end up rechecking the stove, and making sure the front door is locked, just checking it again and again. And I do this thing where I silently count through all my steps before I can actually leave the house. I used to be so punctual, but now these little checks are starting to make me late for everything, even when I know perfectly well I’ve already done enough.

Do you find that these routines are accompanied by particular thoughts or worries that come up while you're doing them, like a fear that something bad might happen if you don't complete the action just right?

Well, yes, exactly. I’ll just be sitting quietly, reading at home—I'm currently going through a rather dense but brilliant biography of William Howard Taft. Most people only remember him for the rumor about getting stuck in a White House bathtub, which is a complete historical fabrication, by the way. His work as Chief Justice later in life was actually his true passion, and I could probably talk about the Taft court all afternoon. 

But... oh, right, the thoughts. Yes, I'll be reading, or maybe getting ready for my volunteer shift down at the local history museum, and suddenly this... this ugly little thought just keeps barging in. It’s this nagging sense that I’ve left something unsafe, or that I’ve touched something unclean, or that I’ve somehow put someone at risk by being careless. And I know perfectly well it’s completely out of proportion! I mean, I'm a rational man. But the thought just sits there. 

Like at the museum, we recently acquired this lovely set of World War I field binoculars, and the leather strap was in such delicate condition, I had to be so careful handling it, and... wait, I'm sorry, I've lost my train of thought. Did that answer what you were asking about the worries?

latest_inference.note: The patient described repetitive behaviors (hand washing, checking routines) and intrusive, unwanted thoughts that cause distress and interfere with daily functioning. These behaviors are aimed at preventing or reducing anxiety or preventing a dreaded event. This is consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder. There is not enough information to rule out other comorbid conditions, but the presentation strongly points toward F42.2 (Mixed obsessional thoughts and acts).
